places.name: Paris home
equipment: Light dumbbells: a 2 kg and a 4 kg pair (or 1 and 2 kg, to confirm)

routines.name: Cycling & ski prep
routines.format: Circuit, 3 rounds. 60–90 s rest between exercises, 2 min between rounds.
warmup: 2 min easy treadmill walk or bike
10 leg swings per leg, front-back and side-side
notes: Add a little weight when the last round still feels moderate.
Skip the finisher if your legs are already shaky; landing quality matters more than volume.

routines.name: Short session
routines.format: Circuit, 3 rounds. 45–60 s rest between exercises.
notes: One squat, one pull, one hinge: the minimum that keeps the main patterns going.

routines.name: Upper body & posture
routines.format: Supersets: do A1 then A2, rest 60–90 s, repeat for 3 rounds. Then B, then C.
warmup: 2 min rowing machine or arm circles
10 band pull-aparts or light rear-delt flys
notes: Pulling volume is at least equal to pushing on purpose: that balance is what helps desk posture.

routines.name: Mobility
routines.equipment: Anywhere: mat, strap or towel, wall
routines.format: One pass, slow and controlled. Breathe out into each stretch. No pain, only stretch.
notes: Good on rest days, after a ride, or as a cooldown after any of the other routines.
The couch stretch targets the hip flexors that stay shortened on the bike and at the desk.

routines.name: Strength + indoor ride
routines.equipment: Gym: dumbbells, bench or box, indoor bike
routines.format: Strength first, then ride. Straight sets with 90–120 s rest: heavier and fewer reps than the circuit days.
warmup: 10 min easy spin, last 2 min a bit brisker
5 per side of the world's greatest stretch
notes: Why strength first: in the off-season the lifting is the priority, and it needs fresh legs for good form. Steady riding is low-skill and tolerates fatigue well.
If a hard interval session is the priority that day, flip the order or do strength on a different day. Don't stack max efforts after heavy legs.
Pick the endurance ride by default and the tempo option at most once a week.

routines.name: Paris home · Strength
routines.equipment: Bands, light dumbbells, mat, foam roller
routines.format: Circuit, 3 rounds, 45 s rest between exercises. The weights are too light to load the legs, so the work comes from one leg at a time and a slow lowering: count 3 seconds down on every rep.
warmup: Foam roll quads and glutes, 30 s each
10 band pull-aparts with the lightest band
4 per side of the world's greatest stretch

items.note: 3 s down. Hold a dumbbell in each hand once bodyweight gets easy.
Heaviest dumbbell in the opposite hand, 3 s down.
Single-leg version, 1 s squeeze at the top.

notes: Progress with harder bands, extra reps or a pause at the bottom, not weight: light dumbbells run out fast for legs.
If you can do 12 slow split squats per leg, hold both dumbbells, or add a fourth round.

split-squat.name: Split squat
setup: Long stride stance: front foot flat, back heel up
Torso tall, hands on hips or dumbbells at the sides
movement: Lower straight down until the back knee almost touches the floor
Take 3 seconds on the way down
Push through the front heel to come up; feet stay planted
All reps on one leg, then switch
cues: Most of the weight on the front leg
Front knee tracks over the toes
Down like an elevator, not forward like a lunge
split-squat.easier: Shorter range, or a hand on a wall for balance
split-squat.harder: Dumbbells, a 2 s pause at the bottom, or 1.5 reps (down, halfway up, down, up)

band-row.name: Seated band row
setup: Sit with legs straight, band looped around the soles of your feet
Hold an end in each hand, arms straight, back tall
movement: Pull the hands to your lower ribs, elbows close to the body
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for 1 s
Return slowly
cues: Don't lean back to finish the rep
Shoulders down, away from the ears
band-row.easier: Lighter band, or knees slightly bent
band-row.harder: Heavier band, or choke up on the band for more tension

band-pull-apart.name: Band pull-apart
setup: Stand tall, band in both hands at shoulder height, arms straight, hands shoulder-width
movement: Pull the band apart until it touches your chest
Pause, then return slowly
cues: Squeeze between the shoulder blades
Ribs down: don't arch the lower back
band-pull-apart.easier: Lighter band, or hands wider apart
band-pull-apart.harder: Heavier band, or hands closer together

foam-thoracic.name: Foam roller thoracic extension
setup: Lie with the roller across your upper back, below the shoulder blades
Hands behind the head, hips on the floor
movement: Let the upper back extend over the roller, breathe out
Roll up a few centimetres and repeat
Stay above the lower ribs
cues: Support the head; don't crank the neck
Don't roll the lower back

goblet-squat.name: Goblet squat
setup: Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest, hands cupping the top end
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
movement: Chest up, core tight
Sit down and back until thighs are about parallel
Elbows track between the knees at the bottom
Push through the whole foot to stand
cues: Dumbbell stays glued to the chest
Knees follow the toes, never cave in
Weight in mid-foot and heels
goblet-squat.easier: Bodyweight, or squat to a bench
goblet-squat.harder: Heavier dumbbell, or a 3 s lowering

sl-rdl.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
setup: Stand on one leg, soft knee
Dumbbell in the opposite hand, or one in each hand for balance
movement: Hinge at the hip, free leg travels straight back
Lower the weight until you feel the hamstring stretch or your back starts to round
Squeeze the glute of the standing leg to come up
cues: A hinge, not a squat: little knee bend
Back leg, torso and arm move as one line
Hips stay square to the floor
sl-rdl.easier: Tap the free foot down between reps, or hold a rack for balance
sl-rdl.harder: Heavier weight, or a pause at the bottom

lateral-lunge.name: Lateral lunge
setup: Feet together, dumbbell at the chest if loaded
movement: Big step to the side
Sit the hips back over the stepping leg; the other leg stays straight
Push off to return to the start
cues: Both feet point forward, heels down
Chest up, hips back like a one-sided squat
lateral-lunge.harder: Goblet hold, or a slide back to centre without stopping

db-row.name: One-arm dumbbell row
setup: Left hand and left knee on the bench, right foot on the floor
Dumbbell in the right hand, back flat and close to parallel
movement: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip
Drive the elbow back and squeeze the shoulder blade
Lower with control, then switch sides after all reps
cues: Elbow to hip, not hand to shoulder
No torso twist
db-row.alt: No bench: bent-over row with two dumbbells, hinged at the hips

wall-sit.name: Wall sit
setup: Back flat on a wall, feet about 60 cm out
movement: Slide down until knees are at about 90°
Hold, breathing steadily
cues: Knees over ankles, not past the toes
Whole back stays on the wall
wall-sit.easier: Sit higher, around 120° at the knee
wall-sit.harder: Dumbbell on the thighs, or longer holds

plank.name: Plank
setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders
Body in one line from head to heels
movement: Hold, breathing normally
cues: Squeeze glutes, tuck ribs down
Hips neither sagging nor piked
plank.harder: Lift one foot, or reach one arm forward alternately

glute-bridge.name: Glute bridge
setup: On your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width
movement: Drive through the heels and lift the hips
Squeeze the glutes for 1 s at the top
Lower slowly
cues: Ribs down: lift with the hips, not by arching the lower back
Knees stay hip-width
glute-bridge.harder: Single-leg: other knee pulled to the chest. Or a dumbbell on the hips

jump-squat.name: Jump squat
setup: Feet shoulder-width
movement: Quarter to half squat, then jump up explosively
Land softly and sink straight into the next rep
cues: Quiet landings, knees out
Stop the set when landings get sloppy
jump-squat.easier: Squat with a calf raise, no jump

bulgarian-split-squat.name: Bulgarian split squat
setup: Rear foot laces-down on a bench behind you
Front foot far enough forward that the shin stays roughly vertical at the bottom
movement: Lower the back knee toward the floor
Push through the front heel to stand
All reps on one leg, then switch
cues: Most of the weight on the front leg
Torso tall, or a slight lean for more glute
bulgarian-split-squat.easier: Bodyweight, or a regular split squat without the bench
bulgarian-split-squat.harder: Dumbbells in both hands, or a 3 s lowering

step-up.name: Step-up
setup: Box at about knee height, dumbbells at the sides
movement: Whole foot on the box, drive up through that heel
Stand tall, then step down with control
cues: Don't push off the back foot
Knee tracks over the toes

push-up.name: Push-up
setup: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line
movement: Lower the chest to the floor, elbows at about 45°
Push back up
cues: Core tight, hips don't sag
push-up.easier: Hands on a bench, or knees down

db-bench-press.name: Dumbbell bench press
setup: Lie on the bench, feet flat, dumbbells over the chest
Shoulder blades pulled back and down
movement: Lower the dumbbells to chest level, elbows at about 45°
Press up until arms are straight
cues: Wrists stacked over elbows
Control the lowering, don't bounce

half-kneeling-press.name: Half-kneeling dumbbell press
setup: Kneel on one knee, other foot in front
Dumbbell at the shoulder on the kneeling-leg side
movement: Press straight up until the arm is locked
Lower slowly back to the shoulder
cues: Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg
Ribs down, no leaning back
half-kneeling-press.harder: Heavier, or a 2 s pause overhead

face-pull.name: Face pull
setup: Rope attachment at about face height
Overhand grip, step back until arms are straight
movement: Pull the rope toward your forehead, splitting the ends apart
Finish with elbows high and hands beside the ears
Return slowly
cues: Light weight, feel the back of the shoulders
Don't lean back to move the weight
face-pull.alt: No cable: bent-over rear-delt fly with light dumbbells

dead-bug.name: Dead bug
setup: On your back, arms straight up, knees bent at 90° above the hips
movement: Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor
Return, then switch sides
cues: Lower back stays pressed into the floor
Exhale as you extend

side-plank.name: Side plank
setup: On your side, forearm on the floor, elbow under shoulder
Feet stacked, or top foot in front for balance
movement: Lift the hips into one straight line, head to feet
Hold
cues: Hips pushed slightly forward, not piked back

cat-cow.name: Cat-cow
setup: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips
movement: Inhale: drop the belly, lift chest and tailbone
Exhale: round the back up, tuck the chin and tailbone
cues: Move one vertebra at a time, slowly

open-book.name: Open book
setup: Lie on your side, knees bent at 90° and stacked, arms straight in front
movement: Sweep the top arm up and over to the other side, following it with your eyes
Let the chest open toward the ceiling, pause, return
cues: Knees stay together on the floor: the rotation comes from the upper back

hip-90-90.name: 90/90 hip switch
setup: Sit with both knees bent at 90°, one leg in front and one to the side
movement: Keeping feet on the floor, rotate both knees to the other side
Sit tall in each position for a breath
cues: Hands behind you for support if needed
Slow, no forcing

worlds-greatest.name: World's greatest stretch
setup: Step into a long lunge, back knee down or hovering
movement: Both hands inside the front foot, drop the elbow toward the instep
Rotate and reach the inside arm to the ceiling
Return the hand, then switch sides
cues: Squeeze the back glute to open the hip flexor

couch-stretch.name: Couch stretch
couch-stretch.equipment: Wall or bench, pad for the knee
setup: Back knee on a pad near the wall, shin up the wall
Front foot planted in a lunge position
movement: Bring the torso upright
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and hold
cues: Tuck the pelvis under; don't arch the lower back
Back off if the knee complains
couch-stretch.easier: Knee further from the wall, hands on the front knee

hamstring-stretch.name: Lying hamstring stretch
setup: On your back, strap around one foot
movement: Raise the straight leg until you feel the stretch
Hold, breathing slowly
cues: Other leg stays long on the floor
Slight knee bend is fine

childs-pose.name: Child's pose
setup: Kneel, big toes together, knees apart
movement: Sit back onto the heels and reach the arms forward
Breathe into the back of the ribs

ride-endurance.name: Endurance ride
movement: Steady effort, conversational pace
Cadence 85–95
cues: You should be able to speak in full sentences
Easy last 5 min

ride-tempo.name: Tempo intervals
movement: After 10 min easy: 3 × 8 min at a comfortably hard effort, 3 min easy between
5 min easy to finish
cues: Short phrases only, but well short of all-out
If the legs are toast from lifting, ride easy instead
